source.title: Same Pre-training Loss, Better Downstream: Implicit Bias Matters for Language Models
source.authors: Hong Liu; Sang Michael Xie; Zhiyuan Li; Teng-Yu Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study uses controlled comparisons of downstream performance at similar pre-training loss, and across model sizes and training steps. It tests downstream predictability with a different setup from the original scaling-law studies, but does not fit or reproduce their power laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on downstream accuracy at similar pre-training losses and as model size or training steps vary. It does not report power-law fits, compute-optimal allocations, or the cited scaling-law results as new experiments.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments show models with the same, near-optimal pre-training loss differing in downstream accuracy across training steps, model size and training algorithm. This bears directly on V6's 'predictable with pretraining loss' arm, and also on its 'improves with scale' arm. It is an argument that V6 needs restating, though it fits no power law.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that pre-training loss cannot fully explain downstream performance. In the saturation regime, continued training, larger size and standard rather than adversarial training each give better downstream results at the same loss, which they attribute to the optimizer's implicit bias. They prove that mini-batch SGD prefers flatter minima and show empirically that flatness correlates with downstream performance. In a Dyck setting they prove that the flattest model transfers.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares downstream outcomes at similar pre-training loss and across model sizes, training steps, and algorithms on simplified datasets; it does not fit scaling laws or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with model size, training steps, training algorithm, dataset, downstream task, and downstream evaluation method (fine-tuning or linear probe).

fits_no_version.finding: The trace of the pre-training-loss Hessian decreases with continued SGD training and with model size, and correlates with downstream accuracy among models of equal loss. In Table 2, the adversarial model's trace is 19.34 vs 8.01 for AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Among models with the same minimal pre-training loss, flatter minima (lower Hessian trace) transfer better downstream.

record.problems: The main experiments use simplified PCFG- and HMM-generated datasets and OPT-generated text restricted to the top-2000 tokens. The authors state that experiments focus on simplified datasets because of computational constraints and leave systematic out-of-distribution evaluation for future work. Several outcomes are only plotted; the OPT checkpoint comparison in Figure 1 has no error bars.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 11 contains further PCFG Task A and Task B and HMM Task-6 checkpoint curves; these additional plotted curves were not extracted separately because Figures 3 and 11 report the same continued-training/flatness pattern for related tasks without additional exact downstream changes in the text.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No quantitative prediction law or fit of downstream vs scale or loss. No real large-scale natural-text corpora; only synthetic PCFG, HMM and OPT-generated data at up to 730M parameters.
No comparison of fitted exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: Fine-tuning accuracy curves across model sizes for PCFG Task B, HMM Task-10 and OPT QNLI. Only the linear-probe gains are recorded.
Pre-saturation segment, where smaller models have higher loss and lower downstream accuracy. Here loss and downstream move together, so loss-predictability holds outside saturation.
missing.locator: Figure 2, left of the dashed saturation line

missing.what: Table 2 trace-of-Hessian values for AdamW (8.01) vs adversarial (19.34).

record.verdict_notes: Tranche is changed to T5 because the paper's purpose is to argue that the loss–downstream link (V6) needs restating. The scale arm of V6 is supported only qualitatively. The loss-arm failure is confined to near-entropy loss on small synthetic datasets, so it is labelled limits_scope rather than challenges. The lookup-table rows are re-linked to none because the lookup table is not a trained LM. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit of held-out pre-training loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to much larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or estimate of compute-optimal parameter and token counts.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law forms across modalities or the listed training regimes.

The study tests downstream accuracy on simplified PCFG- and HMM-generated data and OPT-generated text, not a general quantitative prediction law across large-scale language models or downstream tasks.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations under different fitting choices, and no test of curves bending away from a power law.

relationships.condition: Model-size sweeps (transformers 2M–730M, LSTMs 10M–135M) on PCFG-, HMM- and OPT-generated data, with linear probe and fine-tuning
relationships.reason: Downstream accuracy rises with model size (+6.9%, +4.5%, +2.0% in R3–R5; Figure 9 tasks in R6–R11; 40.4→50.5% in R24; R26). Increases are monotone, but no law is fitted.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream accuracy increased monotonically with model size, including reported gains of 6.9%, 4.5% and 2.0% and an increase from 40.4% to 50.5%, without a fitted scaling law.

relationships.condition: Saturation regime, where pre-training loss is at or near the data entropy, compared across training steps, algorithms and sizes
relationships.reason: At equal loss, downstream differs by 2–7 points: post-convergence gains (R1, R2, R20, R21) and adversarial vs AdamW (R13, R15, R19). So loss alone does not predict downstream in this regime.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream scores differed by 2–7 points at equal loss across training steps, algorithms, and sizes, including improvements after convergence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Models with similar or equal pre-training loss but different training procedures or training steps
